messages:
maria: Heads up — ran an nsys trace on the TRT-vLLM wrapper with a small sample workload. Seeing ~45% of time in wrapper bookkeeping (serialize/deserialize + scheduler handoff) instead of engine kernels.
jon: hmm that's high. can you paste the high-level timeline?
maria: pasted snippet from the timeline: `ENGINE_INVOKE (3ms) -> WRAPPER_COPY_IN (8ms) -> SCHED_ENQUEUE (12ms) -> WRAPPER_COPY_OUT (9ms)` — repeated per token chunk.
kevin: which kernel selection mode was used? autoselect or forced fp16-int8 path?
maria: autoselect. models/1.7B fp16. interestingly when I force a quantized engine the kernel time drops but the wrapper copy times remain.
perfbot: automated note: nsys capture 1945678901, size=1.2GB, events=cudaMemcpyAsync,cudaLaunchKernel,hostToDeviceQueue.
sara: can you share the nsys args you ran? maybe stream syncs are forcing host stalls.
maria: ran `nsys profile -o trace_1945678901 --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none --capture-range=cuda` with venv. capture shows a lot of small cudaMemcpyAsync calls interleaved with kernel launches.
devon: that pattern smells like per-request KV cache copy-on-evict. are we doing a full KV blit on every prefill?
jon: i mean jon: ^ agreed. check whether kvcache prewarm is enabled and whether we accidentally disabled prefix caching in the wrapper.
maria: good call — prefix cache was toggled off in this config for testing. when I re-enable prefix caching the wrapper copy counts drop ~70%.
kevin: still need to explain the 12ms SCHED_ENQUEUE. is the scheduler doing per-token locking? show scheduler trace.
maria: attaching condensed scheduler timeline (copied below):
```
SCHED tick 0: pick engine A (queue len 1)
SCHED tick 1: enqueue task -> lock per-queue
SCHED tick 2: serialize token ctx -> push
SCHED tick 3: awaken worker -> context switch
SCHED tick 4: worker copies KV -> handoff to engine
```
Looks like we do a sync context switch between enqueue and worker wake causing ~8-12ms overhead.
sara: could be the worker thread doing heavy Python GC during serialize. which python runtime? pypy?
maria: CPython 3.10, single procs pinned. we saw GC pauses ~6-8ms in the trace aligned with enqueue.
devon: option: move serialization to a background C-extension or bump to pre-serialized KV objects in shared memory, avoid Python list/dict churn.
jon: before big changes, try batching multiple small requests into one enqueue to amortize the enqueue+copy overhead. what's batching heuristic currently?
maria: it's token-count based with max_batch_size=8 and timeout_ms=10. for this workload (many 1-token hits) it never batches.
kevin: suggest try timeout_ms=30 and max_batch_size=16 for a 5% latency SLO experiment. also run `nvprof --print-gpu-trace` on the quantized engine path and compare kernel occupancy.
maria: will try both changes and re-run traces. I'll post pared-down perfetto links and a smaller nsys capture (200MB) once done. thanks all. :thumbsup:
jon: great, ping when you have the new traces. If duplicate we can schedule a quick pairing to instrument the scheduler code paths.
sara: also add a small microbenchmark that simulates many single-token requests — that'll reproduce the enqueue hotpath deterministically.
maria: on it. follow-up will include commit hash, exact nsys cmd, and before/after flamegraphs.
